About MyStockButler: how it works

By Olivier Lachance · Updated October 30, 2026How a report is made

What is MyStockButler?

MyStockButler, in short

An AI system writes each MyStockButler report: one long research report per public company. It never tells you to buy or sell; the decision is yours. MyStockButler is not a broker or an investment adviser.

  1. Reads the company's filings
  2. Writes 8 chapters
  3. Checks the table numbers
  4. Lists every source

Executive Summary

What the business is

Microsoft sells workplace software, cloud computing, business applications, advertising, devices, games and professional services. Its customers range from consumers and PC makers to employers, developers, advertisers and public institutions. Azure is cloud computing: customers rent processing power, storage, databases and AI services from Microsoft’s data centers. Microsoft 365 subscriptions provide Office, Teams, email, document storage, security and Copilot, its AI assistant. Dynamics, Windows Server, GitHub, LinkedIn, Xbox and search add other recurring, licensed and advertising revenue.

What is in a MyStockButler report?

Eight chapters in the order an analyst works: the company first, the price last. The reports are AI-generated research for information only, not investment advice.

  1. 1

    The business

    What it sells, to whom, and how it makes money.

  2. 2

    The market

    Growing or shrinking, the rivals, and what protects it.

  3. 3

    History and capital decisions

    What it bought and where the money went.

  4. 4

    Management and ownership

    Who runs it, who owns it, how they are paid.

  5. 5

    The numbers

    Revenue, earnings, cash flow and debt over five years.

  6. 6

    Valuation and the stock

    What you pay for each dollar of earnings or cash.

  7. 7

    What comes next

    What management announced, and whether it can pay for it.

  8. 8

    Where the price could go

    Bear, base and bull, and what moves it between them.

Three questions run through every report: does management keep its promises, are insiders buying or selling, and is the dividend paid from cash?

How does MyStockButler work?

An AI system reads what the company publishes and writes the report; for each number in its tables, software opens the cited page and records whether the line is there.

  1. Read the filings

    Annual reports, quarterly results, and filings with the SEC or other regulators.

  2. Fill the tables

    By kind of company: a bank, an insurer and a miner are not measured the same way.

  3. Check the table numbers

    Each keeps its copied line and its page's address, and software checks the line.

  4. Write and cite

    Eight chapters around the tables, every source listed; from October 16, 2026 on, a last AI pass removes plainly untrue statements.

The full method, step by step →

Is MyStockButler legit?

MyStockButler is not a broker or an investment adviser. It is a research-report service with a named person behind it, Olivier Lachance, and the numbers in its tables point to the documents they came from. Three things you can check yourself:

A named author

Olivier Lachance signs the pages, and his LinkedIn profile is public.

Sources you can open

Every report ends with the list of its sources, so you can open the filing behind a number.

A written way to report an error

Every message is read and the number checked against the company's own documents. Corrections

What it is not: a price-alert or trading-signal service, and not investment advice.

Which companies have a report?

751 companies had a report on November 3, 2026: 498 of the S&P 500, the whole S&P/TSX 60, most of the FTSE 100 and the Hang Seng, part of the DAX and CAC 40, and 11 others ordered by users.

You can order a new report on a company listed in the US, Canada, London or Hong Kong. When companies report, the library redoes the biggest ones first. Every report can also be read in French, German or Chinese.

How much does MyStockButler cost?

New accounts get one company's ready report free. No card. After that, Starter is $30 a month and Pro $70 a month, in US dollars; a ready report costs 5 credits and a new report 20.

Questions about MyStockButler

Is MyStockButler investment advice?

No. A report sets out facts, numbers and scenarios with their sources; it never tells you to buy or sell, and the decision is yours.

Are there reviews of MyStockButler?

Not yet: no ratings or user reviews are published. What you can check yourself: the author is named, each report lists its sources, and there is a written way to report an error.

Is MyStockButler the same as The Stock Butler or mStock?

No. MyStockButler (mystockbutler.com) writes research reports, one public company at a time.

Can I read a report before I pay?

Yes: Microsoft's first page opens here with no account.

MyStockButler Research TeamUpdated Nov 3, 2026
Important investment disclaimer

This article is general information, not investment advice. It is not a recommendation to buy, sell or hold any security and it does not take your personal circumstances into account. Analysis date: November 3, 2026. Figures can be outdated after that date; verify material facts and consult a qualified adviser before investing.

Executive Summary

What the business is

Microsoft sells workplace software, cloud computing, business applications, advertising, devices, games and professional services. Its customers range from consumers and PC makers to employers, developers, advertisers and public institutions. Azure is cloud computing: customers rent processing power, storage, databases and AI services from Microsoft’s data centers. Microsoft 365 subscriptions provide Office, Teams, email, document storage, security and Copilot, its AI assistant. Dynamics, Windows Server, GitHub, LinkedIn, Xbox and search add other recurring, licensed and advertising revenue.

Fiscal 2026 revenue was $331.84 billion, including $214.4 billion from Microsoft Cloud. A dollar arrives through subscriptions, usage charges, licenses, advertising, hardware or game purchases. Microsoft then pays engineers, salespeople, data-center operators, chip suppliers, electricity providers, partners and content owners. Profitability rests on recurring software revenue, a large installed base and shared infrastructure. The risk is that AI capacity, processors, power and leases grow faster than profitable customer demand.

The latest quarter and year

In the September 2026 quarter, revenue reached $92.28 billion, up from $77.67 billion a year earlier. Azure revenue grew 48%, while Microsoft 365 commercial cloud revenue grew 17% and paid commercial seats rose 5%. Xbox content and services fell 2%, and Windows OEM revenue fell 27%. Gross margin declined to 67.8% as Azure became a larger, more infrastructure-heavy business. Capital expenditure reached $45.2 billion, leaving computed free cash flow of $18.63 billion. OpenAI commercial arrangements generated $10.0 billion, increasing the importance of that partner.

Fiscal 2026 revenue reached $331.84 billion and operating income $155.24 billion. Azure and other cloud services grew 41%, Dynamics 365 grew 18%, and LinkedIn grew 11%. Xbox content and services fell 5%, while search advertising grew 12%. Investors worry that AI growth may require permanently higher capital spending, lower cloud margins and greater OpenAI exposure.

Who runs it

Satya Nadella is chairman and chief executive; Amy Hood is chief financial officer. Nadella’s fiscal 2026 compensation was $90.63 million, including $77.57 million in stock awards. His performance award weights Azure and the rest of Microsoft Cloud at 35% each. Nadella owns 918,226 common shares and Hood owns 555,396. Diluted shares averaged 7,453 million, down 0.2%.
